title: Future Simple
summary: Talk about what is going to happen — "I'll call you tonight", "It's going to rain".
whyThisTopic: Two ways to say the future, and the choice between them says something: **will** if you're deciding as you speak, **going to** if the plan was already there.

assessmentConfig._note: Temporarily 2 for faster testing — production value is 3. questionsPerSubSkill and qualifyingScore must move together: if qualifying > drawn, nobody can ever skip a sub-skill.

blocks.text: For **will**, put **not** straight after it — **will not**, usually shortened to **won't**. For **going to**, the **not** goes after **am / is / are** instead.
subject + will

blocks.label: Watch out
blocks.text: **don't** and **doesn't** have no place here. **He doesn't will come** is wrong — it's **He won't come**.

blocks.label: ব্যাখ্যা
blocks.text: **will**-এর ঠিক পরে **not** বসে — **will not**, সংক্ষেপে **won't**। **going to**-এর ক্ষেত্রে **not** বসে **am / is / are**-এর পরে। এখানে **don't / doesn't** ব্যবহার হয় না।

practice.prompt: Which sentence uses the negative form correctly?

options.text: I won't tell anyone.

feedback.en: Correct. **not** goes straight after **will**, and **will not** shortens to **won't**.
feedback.bn: ঠিক আছে। **will**-এর ঠিক পরে **not** বসে; **will not** সংক্ষেপে **won't**।

options.text: I don't will tell anyone.

feedback.en: **don't / doesn't** belongs to the present simple, and never sits next to **will**.
feedback.bn: **don't / doesn't** present simple-এর, আর এটি **will**-এর পাশে বসে না।

options.text: I won't tells anyone.

feedback.en: After **won't**, the verb stays plain — no **-s**, no **-ing**.
feedback.bn: **won't**-এর পরে verb-এর base form থাকে — **-s** বা **-ing** নয়।

options.text: I not will tell anyone.

feedback.en: **not** goes straight after **will**, not before it.
feedback.bn: **not** **will**-এর ঠিক পরে বসে, আগে নয়।

feedback.en: The right idea, but the wrong form of **be** for this subject.

feedback.en: After **going to** comes the plain verb, even in the negative.
feedback.bn: না-বোধকেও **going to**-এর পরে base form বসে।

blocks.text: For **will**, move it in front of the subject. For **going to**, it's **am / is / are** that moves instead — **going to** stays where it is.
Will + subject + plain verb

items.text: Is she going to buy it?

blocks.label: Watch out
blocks.text: Never use **do** or **does**. **Do you will come?** is wrong — it's **Will you come?**

blocks.label: ব্যাখ্যা
blocks.text: **will** দিয়ে প্রশ্ন করতে **will** subject-এর আগে বসে। **going to**-এর ক্ষেত্রে **am / is / are** আগে বসে। **What / When / Where** থাকলে সেটি সবার আগে: **When will they meet?** এখানে **do / does** ব্যবহার হয় না।

options.text: Does she will sing tonight?

feedback.en: **Do / Does** is for the present simple. This question starts with **Will**.
feedback.bn: **Do / Does** present simple-এর। এই প্রশ্ন **Will** দিয়ে শুরু হয়।

options.text: She will sing tonight?

feedback.en: That's a statement with a question mark. In a question, **will** comes before the subject.
feedback.bn: এটি প্রশ্ন নয়, শুধু শেষে প্রশ্নবোধক চিহ্ন। প্রশ্নে **will** subject-এর আগে বসে।

options.text: Will she sing tonight?

feedback.en: Correct. **Will** moves in front of the subject, and nothing else changes.
feedback.bn: ঠিক আছে। **Will** subject-এর আগে চলে আসে, বাকি সব একই থাকে।

options.text: Will she sings tonight?

feedback.en: Questions keep the plain verb after **will** too.
feedback.bn: প্রশ্নেও **will**-এর পরে base form থাকে।

blocks.text: Both talk about the future, but they start from different places. **will** is for a decision you make as you speak. **going to** is for a plan you already had, or something you can see coming.
deciding as you speak → will
blocks.highlight: already planned, or visible → going to

rows: I'm going to buy a car.

items.text: The phone's ringing — I'll get it.
I'm going to buy a car next month.
Look at those clouds — it's going to snow.

blocks.label: Watch out
blocks.text: Neither one is wrong English. The difference is **when you decided** — **will** if you're deciding as you speak, **going to** if the plan was already there.

blocks.label: ব্যাখ্যা
blocks.text: দুইটিই ভবিষ্যৎ বোঝায়; পার্থক্য হলো **কখন সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়া হয়েছে**। কথা বলার মুহূর্তে সিদ্ধান্ত নিলে **will**; আগে থেকেই পরিকল্পনা থাকলে, বা ঘটনাটি চোখের সামনে ঘটতে দেখলে **going to**।

practice.prompt: A waiter is waiting and you choose your dish on the spot. Which sentence fits best?

options.text: I'm going to take the fish.

feedback.en: **going to** says the plan already existed. This decision is being made right now, so it's **will**.
feedback.bn: **going to** বোঝায় পরিকল্পনা আগে থেকেই ছিল। এখানে সিদ্ধান্ত এই মুহূর্তে নেওয়া হচ্ছে, তাই **will** বসে।

options.text: I will to take the fish.

feedback.en: No **to** after **will** — the plain verb follows it directly.
feedback.bn: **will**-এর পরে **to** বসে না; সরাসরি verb-এর base form বসে।

options.text: I will taking the fish.

feedback.en: **-ing** belongs to the continuous tenses. After **will**, use the plain verb.
feedback.bn: **-ing** continuous tense-এর। **will**-এর পরে base form বসে।

options.text: I'll take the fish.

feedback.en: Correct. You're deciding as you speak, and that's what **will** is for.
feedback.bn: ঠিক আছে। কথা বলার মুহূর্তে সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়া হচ্ছে — এখানেই **will** বসে।

practice.prompt: You decided weeks ago and the buyer is coming tomorrow. Which sentence fits best?

options.text: I'm going to sell my bike.

feedback.en: Correct. The plan already existed before you spoke, so it's **going to**.
feedback.bn: ঠিক আছে। পরিকল্পনাটি আগে থেকেই ছিল, তাই **going to** বসে।

options.text: I going to sell my bike.

feedback.en: **going to** can't stand on its own — it needs **am**, **is** or **are** in front of it.
feedback.bn: **going to** একা বসতে পারে না — এর আগে **am / is / are** লাগে।

options.text: I'll sell my bike.

feedback.en: **will** sounds like you're deciding this second. The plan was already made, so it's **going to**.
feedback.bn: **will** শুনলে মনে হয় এই মুহূর্তে সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়া হচ্ছে। পরিকল্পনা আগেই ছিল, তাই **going to** বসে।

options.text: I am going to selling my bike.

feedback.en: After **going to** comes the plain verb, never the **-ing** form.
feedback.bn: **going to**-এর পরে base form বসে, **-ing** form নয়।

practice.prompt: The glass is rocking at the edge of the shelf. Which sentence fits best?

options.text: It'll break.

feedback.en: **will** is for a guess with nothing in front of you. Here you can see it happening, so it's **going to**.
feedback.bn: **will** এমন অনুমানের জন্য যার কোনো প্রমাণ সামনে নেই। এখানে ঘটনাটি চোখের সামনে, তাই **going to** বসে।

options.text: It going to break.

feedback.en: **going to** can't stand on its own — it needs **am**, **is** or **are** in front of it.
feedback.bn: **going to** একা বসতে পারে না — এর আগে **am / is / are** লাগে।

options.text: It's going to break.

feedback.en: Correct. You can see it coming, and English uses **going to** for that.
feedback.bn: ঠিক আছে। ঘটনাটি চোখের সামনে আসছে — এমন ক্ষেত্রে **going to** বসে।

options.text: It is going to breaking.

feedback.en: After **going to** comes the plain verb, never the **-ing** form.
feedback.bn: **going to**-এর পরে base form বসে, **-ing** form নয়।
